COMPANY
Alpha Impulsion was founded in 2022 and is 12 people strong as of 2025 in Toulouse, with 3 additional collaborators in the Torino subsidiary. The founding element is a patent on hybrid autophage propulsion, a rocket propulsion technology applicable to launchers, in-space thrusters and missiles. The architecture proposes to use a solid fuel to as the launcher's fuselage and tank for its liquid oxidiser, and to burn this propellant rod like a candle. This disruptive technology removes the need for tanks, which, for instance, represent half the dry mass of a launcher, enabling a single-stage-to-orbit (SSTO) trajectory. Similar benefits are found in other applications. The mass reduction and overall reduction in parts number allows significant savings in manufacturing and logistics.

COMMERCIAL AIM
The company aims to commercialize several products and services ased on the autophage technology:
- OPAL, a versatile, storable in-space chemical propulsion subsystem for high thrust, high ΔV needs using H2O2. The pre-design for the Shakthisat mission (https://www.shakthisat.org/) with a non-clustered OPAL of circa 200kg shows an improvement of 40% in spacecraft payload capacity for a moon mission propelled by autophage propulsion from LEO. This also leads to savings at launch. 
- GRENAT, a launch service for satellites with the lowest environmental footprint. Pre-design shows that the launch event uses circa 40% less propellant mass than competing technologies (Gros et al., 2023, https://hal.science/hal-04704331). The launch service is dedicated to smallsats with a target capacity of 1000kg (SSO 500km), as opposed to rideshare, and is able to compete on price due to the simplification in manufacturing and logistics brought by the SSTO architecture and miniaturisation. This will allow this European launcher to compete with advantages against the American leader that currently dominates the European smallsat launch market. Reusing the launcher is not necessary for these goals, and represents an improvement.

R&D STAGE
From 2023 to 2025, the company developed AMBRE, the first hybrid autophage propulsion demonstrator, and ran several test campaign with progressive subsystems integration. In 2024, the combustion chamber was fired and the fuselage feeding system was developed. In 2025, TRL3 was validated with the largest autophage engine ever fired, demonstrating the functions of inserting the fuselage with its liquid oxidant into the combustion chamber and burning them, with modest funding. Alpha Impulsion aims to achieve the technological breakthroughwith with an increasing number of European partners. Next steps include engineering models in the development of OPAL, and scaling up the engine prototype for the launcher roadmap with the University of Glasgow, the leading academic actor in autophage combustion, and other key partners in structural mechanics and GNC.

entityDescription:
ACTeon is a human size research and consultancy that supports ecological and climate transitions in Europe. ACTeon works in a wide range of policy domains, addressing sustainability and resilience related to freshwater, marine ecosystems, coastal management, biodiversity or transversal climate change adaptation issues. ACTeon is involved in projects and initiatives from the local to the European (e.g. European Commission, European Environment Agency, WWF European Policy Office...) and international levels (OECD, United Nations...), mobilising human science knowledge and tools for investigating social and economic issues, carrying out policy evaluation, supporting forward looking processes, analysing governance and institutions, or supporting stakeholder processes and communication. Overall, ACTeon has strong expertise in awareness raising, capacity building and communication to a diversity of target groups, and in the facilitation of stakeholder processes at all scales bringing together a diversity of views and opinions. 
ACTeon works in particular on maritime and marine issues with expertise and experiences related to: (a) social and economic assessments (e.g. social challenges related to marine policy implementation valuation of services provided by marine ecosystems, growth and employment impacts of Blue economy sectors, costs and benefits of the MSFD…); (b) the upscaling of innovations (e.g. nature-based solutions, bioeconomy, the role of algae to address climate change challenges, multi-use platforms at sea); (c) ocean literacy and drivers to behaviour change (e.g. coordination of EU4Ocean coalition for strengthening ocean literacy). (d) (a) EU policy, strategies and management (e.g. the EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive, Maritime Spatial Planning, Integrated Coastal Zone Management, Sustainable Blue Economy…); (e) governance (regional sea basin and international Ocean Governance scales) including the “blue” science-policy-society interface and how knowledge effectively support policy making and implementation;

description:
The first GHGSat satellite was launched in 2016 as a demo that measured surface-level methane emission plumes with high spatial resolution. Fast forward to 2023, GHGSat operates the largest constellation of methane detecting satellites at high resolution (12 by end of 2023). 
The patented instrument is a wide-angle fixed-cavity Fabry–Pérot (F–P) imaging spectrometer able to resolve methane (CH4) absorption lines in the shortwave infrared (SWIR), where water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2) absorption lines are also present. GHGSat satellites are Polar, sun-synchronous, with local times at des. node between 09:00h and 14:00h, at an altitude of ~500km.
 The distinguishing features of GHGSat satellites are its combination of high spatial resolution (25 m), fine spectral resolution (~ 0.1 nm) and compact package. To this day the GHGSat satellites remain the only greenhouse gas sensing satellites with such characteristics. This combination enables unique capabilities for imaging and quantifying emission plumes with unambiguous attribution at facility scale, with a industry leading detection threshold of ~100kg/h.
At company level, GHGSat counts +110 employees, with a team of +12 scientist working full-time in advancing the science of remote sensing of methane beyond the state-of-the-art, having been successful in R&D projects with renowned institutions such as CSA, ESA, NASA, Stanford and SRON. GHGSat data is part of ESA TPM program from 2021, and NASA's CSDA from 2023.
